newEntriesNeeded.title: PMLTAGS object and exportasxls method
newEntriesNeeded.principle: The PMLTAGS object provides methods to query and export engineering tag data to spreadsheet formats.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Create a PMLTAGS instance with `object PMLTAGS()`, then call `.exportasxls(!groupName, !listName, !filePath)` to export matching tags.
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- Export tags from a named list
!!tags = object PMLTAGS()
var !grid collect all LSTDEF with (LSTNAM eq |my-list|)
if (!grid.size() eq 1) then
    !gridRef = !grid.first().dbref()
    var !gName CATNAM of LSTGRP of $!gridRef
    !!tags.exportasxls(!gName, '$!<gridRef.LSTNAM>', '$!outPath')
endif
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- Don't reuse PMLTAGS across different export contexts without clearing
!!tags = object PMLTAGS()
!!tags.exportasxls(...)
!!tags.exportasxls(...) -- stale state may cause wrong export
pitfalls: PMLTAGS is specific to AVEVA Engineering; it may not be available in PDMS-only environments.
The exportasxls method requires valid group and list names; passing empty strings causes runtime errors.

newEntriesNeeded.title: inset operator for list membership in PML1 queries
newEntriesNeeded.principle: The `inset` operator tests whether a value is a member of a list of values in PML1 query expressions.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Use `value inset (list1, list2, ...)` in PML1 query expressions to test membership. Combine with `NOT` to exclude values.
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- Exclude tags with VOID or Future status
!tagFilter = 'NOT(:TagStatus inset (|VOID|, |Future|)) and ISNAMED'
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- Don't use inset with PML2 method chaining
!status.inset(...) -- incorrect, use infix form
pitfalls: inset is a PML1 infix operator; it works inside query expression strings but not in PML2 object method chains.
Values inside inset must be pipe-delimited strings.

newEntriesNeeded.title: LSTDEF and LSTGRP objects for list management
newEntriesNeeded.principle: LSTDEF (List Definition) and LSTGRP (List Group) are AVEVA Engineering objects used to manage named lists for tag data grouping.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Query LSTDEF to find a list by name. Access LSTGRP via `LSTGRP of` to get the group. Use CATNAM to get the group name. Set lstflt to clear filters.
newEntriesNeeded.syntax:
var !grid collect all LSTDEF with (LSTNAM eq |listName|)
!gridRef = !grid.first().dbref()
!gridRef.lstflt = !realUnset
var !gName CATNAM of LSTGRP of $!gridRef
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- Find and clear a list
var !grid collect all LSTDEF with (LSTNAM eq |IM-tag-dataset|)
if (!grid.size() eq 1) then
    !gridRef = !grid.first().dbref()
    !gridRef.lstflt = ARRAY()
    var !gName CATNAM of LSTGRP of $!gridRef
endif
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern: -- Don't assume grid.size() == 1; always check before accessing first()
pitfalls: LSTDEF/LSTGRP are Engineering-specific; not available in PDMS.
lstflt is a reference attribute; setting it to an empty ARRAY clears the filter.

newEntriesNeeded.title: DATETIME object with .string() format codes
newEntriesNeeded.principle: The OBJECT DATETIME() construct returns a datetime object with methods for year, month, date, hour, minute, second. Each can be formatted via .string(formatCode).
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Use `.string('I2')` for zero-padded 2-digit integers, `.string('I4')` for 4-digit years. Format codes follow PDMS/E3D FORMAT conventions.
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- Build a timestamped filename
!dt = OBJECT DATETIME()
!ts = !dt.year().string() & '-' & !dt.month().string('I2') & '-' & !dt.date().string('I2')
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- Don't use .string() without format code for zero-padding
!month = !dt.month().string() -- may produce single-digit '3' instead of '03'
pitfalls: Format codes like 'I2' are PDMS/E3D FORMAT codes; their exact behavior may vary by product version.
.year() returns a REAL; .string() on a bare REAL may not zero-pad.

newEntriesNeeded.title: matchwild function in PML1 query expressions
newEntriesNeeded.principle: The `matchwild` function in PML1 query expressions performs wildcard pattern matching on attribute values or names.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Use `matchwild(attribute, |pattern|)` inside PML1 query expression strings. Supports `*` (any chars) and `?` (single char).
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- Find tags matching a pattern
!tagFilter = 'ISNAMED and matchwild(name, |*GB.*|)'
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- Don't use matchwild as a STRING method in query strings
matchwild(!name, |*|) -- incorrect, use PML1 infix form
pitfalls: matchwild in query strings is PML1-style; the STRING.MatchWild() method is PML2-style. They are not interchangeable in query expression strings.
Variable interpolation in matchwild patterns requires `$!var` syntax inside pipe strings.
